clue.text: Support lord audibly

indicators.note: audibly tells us to go by how the word for a lord sounds when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, such as a lord

explanation.surface: Someone backs a nobleman out loud in a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a supporting pillar or column, as under a bridge or arch.

clue.text: At university time for the latest news

parts.note: UP means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A student at college decides it is time to catch up on current events.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is a report bringing someone up to date with the most recent information.

clue.text: Criticise success that comes through lots of tricks

definitions.meaning: to criticise harshly, as a reviewer might pan a play

definitions.text: success that comes through lots of tricks
definitions.meaning: in bridge, a grand or small ... is won by taking all or all but one of the tricks

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a winner whose success came only through trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricks' sounds like deceit, but it is the bridge sense: the rounds of play a side takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Slam is an informal verb for attacking harshly in words, and also the bridge term for taking nearly every trick.

clue.text: Dissolute priest I found lacking energy and enthusiasm

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, so these letters are set loose and rearranged
lacking tells us one letter is dropped from the word for a clergyman

parts.note: taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for energy in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: A debauched clergyman confesses he has lost all his drive and zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes E (energy) from PRIEST, leaving PRIST; 'Dissolute' rearranges PRIST plus I to make the answer. 'found' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit is liveliness, courage or keenness, so it is a synonym for enthusiasm.

clue.text: Calm knight leading queen into path

indicators.note: into tells us the knight-and-queen pair is placed inside the word for a path

parts.note: a trail is a path or track

indicators.note: leading means the knight comes in front of the queen

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A serene knight escorts his queen onto a woodland path.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranquil means peaceful and untroubled, a direct synonym of calm.

clue.text: False idol of French clan brandished in game

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled letters are put inside the name of a game

parts.note: golf is a game played with clubs and balls
DE is French for of

indicators.note: brandished means waved about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan waves weapons during a round of golf, worshipping a false god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brandished' rearranges DE plus CLAN into DENCAL, which goes 'in' GOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden calf was the idol the Israelites worshipped in the Bible, so it stands for any false god.

clue.text: Management of river in Norfolk town adjoining a lake

indicators.note: adjoining means the following pieces come straight after
in places the river's name inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England
the Po is the longest river in Italy
L is a common abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Running the river in a Norfolk town next to a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal can mean arrangement or control, as in 'at your disposal', so it fits management.

clue.text: Run away from snaky character, one who finds fault

parts.note: the letter S is shaped like a snake
a carper is someone who complains about trivial things

explanation.surface: A frightened person flees a snake-like nagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarper is British slang meaning to flee or run off quickly.

clue.text: Bird arrives diving into grass

indicators.note: diving into tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: pot and grass are both slang for cannabis
ARR is the abbreviation for arrives in timetables

explanation.surface: A bird lands and plunges into the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a brightly coloured tropical bird known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Scoundrel, in the course of time, makes mistakes

indicators.note: in the course of suggests one piece sits within the span of another

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Over time, a villain inevitably slips up.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in a printed work, so the word means mistakes.

clue.text: Soldier receiving notice in a pickle

indicators.note: receiving means the soldier takes in the notice

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with the navy
an ad is a notice advertising something

explanation.surface: A soldier is handed his notice and finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pickle' reads as 'in trouble'; only 'pickle' defines, and 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid for steeping food, much as a pickle is.

clue.text: Nutter in pother bungled car manoeuvre

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lunatic in a commotion botches a turn in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' rearranges NUTTERINPOTHER; pother is an old word for a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-point turn is the standard way of turning a car round in a narrow road, tested in the British driving test.

clue.text: Unsentimental, as a boxer taking some punches needs to be?

definitions.meaning: practical and unemotional, not swayed by feeling

definitions.text: as a boxer taking some punches needs to be?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a fighter who takes blows to the face would want a tough skull

explanation.surface: A boxer who soaks up blows must be tough-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-headed means shrewd and practical, and literally describes a skull able to withstand blows.

clue.text: Poem I set down with a twist in it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a twist inside the word means a letter is shifted within it

parts.note: laid means placed or set down

explanation.surface: A poet puts down his verse with an unexpected twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a twist in it' moves the A of LAID one place on, making LIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War.

clue.text: Harvest to get hold of round end of September

indicators.note: round means the word for seizing goes around a letter

parts.note: to cop is slang for to catch or get hold of

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: Farmers must gather everything in by late September.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is the produce gathered at harvest time.

clue.text: Writer has article about a sorrowful American city

indicators.note: has means the article follows the writer directly
about tells us the writer-plus-article goes around the next pieces

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
taken as written
sad means sorrowful
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An author writes a gloomy piece about life in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the writer-with-article around the inner pair, splitting the writer after its first letter; 'has' just joins the article on.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in California, near Los Angeles.

clue.text: English residing in opulent German state

indicators.note: residing in means one piece lives inside another

parts.note: opulent means rich and luxurious

explanation.surface: An Englishman lives in luxury in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Reich is the German word for empire or realm, used of the German state.

clue.text: Linger outside an industrial city in Germany

indicators.note: outside means the word for lingering wraps around the short word

parts.note: to hover is to linger or hang about
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loiters on the edge of a German factory town.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover is a large city in northern Germany known for trade fairs and industry.

clue.text: King articulate but no leader

indicators.note: no leader tells us to remove the first letter of the word

parts.note: clear means articulate, easily understood

explanation.surface: A monarch is eloquent but has no one to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear is the king in Shakespeare's tragedy King Lear.

clue.text: Family team was behind a fund for restoration

indicators.note: restoration means rebuilding, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple backed a fund to restore an old building.
explanation.definitionFit: A married couple working together is often called a family team.

clue.text: Short financial statement — something that may bind agreement

parts.note: AC (a/c) is the short form of account, a financial statement
a cord is a string used to tie things

explanation.surface: A brief balance sheet tied up with string seals a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal agreement or treaty.

clue.text: Person in cafe — one has got soaked apparently!

indicators.note: has got signals that the water holds the letter for one

parts.note: being soaked means being in water
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A server has been drenched, by the look of it.
explanation.walkthrough: One (I) 'has got soaked': it sits in WATER. 'apparently' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiter serves food and drink to customers in a cafe.

clue.text: Help one to get better for special type of race

parts.note: a hand is help, as in lend a hand
I is the Roman numeral for one
to cap is to outdo or improve on

explanation.surface: Coaching someone to improve before a special event.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a race in which runners carry weights to even out their chances.

clue.text: Group of Scouts prepare for camp?

definitions.meaning: the Cub Scouts are organised into troops of that name
to put belongings into bags before a trip

explanation.surface: A troop of Scouts get ready for camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack is a group of Cub Scouts, and to pack is to fill a bag for travel.

clue.text: Expresses love when restricted by bad habits

indicators.note: restricted by means the letter is confined inside the other word

parts.note: vices are bad habits
O means love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone declares love while held back by his own failings.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice something is to express it, so voices means expresses.

clue.text: One is not fair

definitions.meaning: the number one is odd, so it lacks this quality
fair in the sense of balanced or level

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone has been treated unjustly.
explanation.definitionFit: An even number divides by two, which one cannot, and even means fair or equal.

clue.text: To wander round losing daughter is more despicable

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word for wandering

parts.note: to meander is to wander about aimlessly

explanation.surface: Drifting away from your daughter is a shabby thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaner means nastier or more contemptible, the comparative of mean.

clue.text: Hurried, always getting worried about it

indicators.note: about it means the word for worried goes around the other piece

parts.note: cared can mean worried or felt concern
e'er is the poetic short form of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Someone always rushes about in a state of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along headlong, so careered means hurried.
